interest: Shows consular disaster response in 1930s Japan: verifying American safety, relaying FDR and Hull's condolences, and weighing Red Cross aid.
overview: This file comprises State Department 'List of Papers' (docket and purport catalog sheets) from Record Group 59 (decimal file 894.48 and related sub-files) documenting official U.S. reporting and diplomatic correspondence concerning four major disasters in Japan between 1930 and 1934: the July 1930 typhoon in Nagasaki and southern Japan, the March 1933 Sanriku earthquake and tsunami affecting Iwate, Miyagi, and northern Honshu prefectures, the catastrophic March 1934 conflagration in Hakodate, and the September 1934 Muroto typhoon that devastated Osaka, Kobe, and the wider Kansai region. Across these crises, the documents index communications between the Department of State in Washington, the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo (under Ambassador Joseph C. Grew and Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville), and regional consulates in Nagasaki, Kobe, and Harbin, as well as the American National Red Cross. The indexed correspondence focuses primarily on ascertaining the safety and property of American citizens and missionaries, coordinating formal messages of sympathy between heads of state and foreign ministers, assessing severe municipal and maritime infrastructure damage, and evaluating whether international relief offers were appropriate or might carry unwanted political complications.

subfiles.about: Docket list of State Department correspondence regarding the March 1933 Sanriku earthquake and tsunami in Iwate Prefecture and northern Honshu.
subfiles.summary: Indexes reports on the March 1933 Iwate-area earthquake and tidal wave: no American casualties, Japanese officials given U.S. sympathy messages.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Earthquake - Iwate, Japan

subfiles.about: Docket list of State Department papers concerning the catastrophic conflagration that destroyed the city of Hakodate in March 1934.
subfiles.summary: Indexes reports on the March 1934 Hakodate fire: heavy loss of life, no American casualties, condolences exchanged with Japan.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Destruction of the City of Hakodate, Japan, by Fire

subfiles.about: Docket list of State Department papers concerning the July 1930 typhoon that caused extensive destruction in Nagasaki and southern Japan.
subfiles.summary: Indexes reports on the July 1930 Nagasaki typhoon: over 100 million yen damage, no American deaths, Red Cross relief contacts.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Typhoon - Nagasaki, Japan - 1930

subfiles.about: Two-page docket list of State Department papers concerning the devastating September 1934 Muroto typhoon in Osaka and the Kansai region.
subfiles.summary: Covers the September 21, 1934 Osaka typhoon: Kobe despatches detail Kansai damage and port destruction, confirm American residents safe, record FDR's condolences to Emperor Hirohito, and note caution against the Red Cross appearing overly eager to offer aid.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Typhoon - Osaka, Japan, September, 1934
